newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian Oil, Petronas in parallel LPG deal.
newsitem.headline: Indian Oil, Petronas in parallel LPG deal.

text.p: State-run Indian Oil Corp plans to enter the parallel market for domestic sale of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) with Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) of Malaysia, an IOC official said on Monday.
"Indian Oil and Petronas have signed a memorandum of understanding to undertake import, storage and sale of bulk and packed LPG," the official, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters.

The proposed IOC-Petronas joint venture, to be set up with 900 million rupees ($25 million) of capital, will annually import 600,000 tonnes of LPG at Haldia in the eastern state of West Bengal, he said.
IOC currently sells packed LPG in cylinders under the brand name Indane.
The price to consumers, fixed under the government's administered price regime, is about two thirds of the cost to IOC. The government makes up the difference to IOC through a subsidy programme.
The IOC-Petronas joint venture will be able to import and sell LPG at market prices, in parallel with subsidised Indane.

Currently only state-run Bharat Petroleum Corp Ltd (BPCL) carries out parallel marketing of LPG. It tied up with Shell Overseas Investment BV, a subsidiary of Royal Dutch/Shell, in 1993 for the sale of LPG under the brand name Shell Gas.
BPCL sells subsidised LPG through the public distribution network under the brand name Bharat Gas.
-- Amitav Ranjan, New Delhi newsroom +91-11 301 2024 ($1 = 35.7 rupees)
